Keystone: after any TAKETHIS line on a peer session the next wire event is an :article (or the close), so no article line is ever a command. scenario: A streaming peer (INN with laxmid, or any sender whose Message-ID is over 250 octets or outside fn-af-msg-id-corep) sends 'TAKETHIS <odd id>' then the article. fn answers 501, then reads every header and body line as a command on the PEER session: each draws a reply the sender maps onto its later outstanding CHECK/TAKETHIS (the stream desynchronises, answers land on the wrong Message-IDs), and a body line such as 'TAKETHIS <x@y>' starts a new transfer whose article is the rest of the body (dot-unstuffed), stored as relayed from that peer. The article's author, not the peer, chooses those lines.
title: TAKETHIS whose argument fails fn's Message-ID grammar is answered 501 and its article is then executed line by line as commands on the peer session
